result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.edge_expansion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the edge expansion of a set of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L51253-L51312){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_expansion( S, T=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge expansion](/assets/graphs/edge-expansion.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S. Three edges cross the cut (accent) and the smaller side by node count is S, with 3 nodes against 4, so the edge expansion is 3 / 3 = 1.0 crossing edge per member." width="100%"} Edge expansion is the cut size divided by the number of nodes on the smaller side: `cut / min(|S|, |T|)`. It measures how many edges leave a set per member. The smallest edge expansion over all sets (the Cheeger constant) tells how well connected a graph is as a whole: expander graphs, where every set has many outgoing edges, are robust and mix random walks quickly. `T` defaults to the complement of `S`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One set of nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The other set. If `None` (default), all nodes not in `S`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights in the cut. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edge expansion. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` or `T=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} One edge leaves each triangle of the two-triangle graph, shared by three nodes: ::: {#2aaba313 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) round(graph.edge_expansion(["A", "B", "C"]), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.333 ``` ::: :::
